parakeet: How is it that a book supposedly written or inspired by an all-knowing, all-powerful God is so unclear that even his most devoted followers can't agree on what it actually says? Wouldn't an all-wise, all-loving deity make sure his most important message was crystal clear? And before you say, well, people just misinterpret it, ask yourselves, if millions of people are misinterpreting it, then isn't that a design flaw? Because God could have done literally anything to make sure his word was unmistakable. He could have written it in the sky. He could have embedded it into human DNA. He could have made it impossible to misunderstand. Instead, we have a collection of ancient texts copied by scribes, translated by committees, edited by religious councils, and used to justify completely opposite beliefs. So either God is a terrible communicator, or maybe this book just isn't divine at all. Because if the Bible was truly the perfect word of God, there wouldn't be 40,000 different ways to read it.
